Systems Touched
M9/M8. Weld modular parts (engine/armor/wheels/boosters/zombie-smash) to car OR motorcycle chassis; parts modify M9 physics.
M9. Player grabs/moves/welds ANY Jolt body (debris, corpses, props); weld-to-vehicle.
M9/M2. Shoot from vehicles — driver leans, passenger fires, recoil/aim while moving.
M9/M8. Weld weapons/guns/spikes onto vehicle frames. END-GAME hard content.
M9/M4. Every car starts broken; rare working ones are side-quest rewards. Hard to earn.
M9/M8. Finite gas; car/wheel durability degrades with use/combat; repair at settlement or roadside.
M9/M8. Attaching a part to a chassis is a hands-on welding minigame: keep the bead inside the tolerance band (metal) or drive fasteners on-mark (wood); quality sets joint strength.
M9. Starting a dead car is a patience/observation minigame: read the loom, find the live + starter wires by color/audio cue, bridge them without shorting — wrong pair sparks, draws zombies.
M9/M2. Picking a lock is a tension + pin-state puzzle: set each pin without over-lifting; one slip drops the pick and alerts. Harder and more contextual than Fallout.
M9/M2. Cracking a door control panel / drone / safe controller is a logic puzzle sibling to lockpicking: route a signal through the circuit node grid without tripping the alarm.
M9/M2. Lifting items from NPCs is a timing/positioning interaction: stay behind, match their rhythm, grab — get caught and standing drops (M8-EXT-53).
M9/M8. A thrown molotov ignites a fuel pool that burns zombies and the environment; damage routed through existing fire physics (M8-EXT-24/30).
